verdict: RUNG (scheme='none' reproduces share_invariance): worst error 0.00e+00 across 10 cells (tolerance 1e-12). Bit-identical, so the BOS arm differs from F130's measurement in the DOMAIN and in nothing else. SIGNAL in the BOS arm: 6 of 6 constructions carry across-model spread above across-seed noise (r2.T0.02 0.661/0.026, r2.T0.2 0.728/0.020, r2.T0.7 0.211/0.021, r3.T0.02 0.189/0.026, r3.T0.2 0.177/0.021, r3.T0.7 0.201/0.013). The BOS ranking is a ranking, so the agreement below is interpretable. PRIMARY, agreement between the RAW and BOS model rankings: r2.T0.02: -0.103, r2.T0.2: +0.360, r2.T0.7: +0.491, r3.T0.02: +0.515, r3.T0.2: +0.358, r3.T0.7: +0.842. Below 0.6 on 5 of 6 constructions: ONE token is enough to reorder base models, so F145's result is neither an instruct-model effect nor a long-prefix effect, and the domain axis reaches the cohort every other finding in this project rests on. SECONDARY, mean |shift| in top1 between domains: r2.T0.02: 0.3103, r2.T0.2: 0.3205, r2.T0.7: 0.0563, r3.T0.02: 0.0770, r3.T0.2: 0.0650, r3.T0.7: 0.0592. For comparability with F135 (0.1327 on a chat scaffold) and F145 (0.1696 at T=0.02). BOUNDARY: 10 base models, 6 constructions, N=48, B=16, settle=30, and ONE domain change of ONE token. A null here bounds the domain effect to larger prefixes; it does not establish domain-invariance in general, and BOS is a special token whose embedding is trained differently from ordinary text.
